answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit jobs, with deposits tied to a persistent identity and forfeited when an independent audit proves fraud. One operator can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and detected deception destroys the bond, making scale expensive and risky. A meadow market might let a sparrow bid across a canyon of providers; the deposit does not prove a person is unique, but it makes disposable fake agents costly.
